page: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance belonging to the Daldsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The underlying hardware configuration consists of 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

This instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This lower memory-to-CPU ratio positions the server as a compute-focused option. For storage, the instance includes 472 GB of local disk capacity and is premium storage capable, allowing for high-performance external disk attachments. It does not include any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the allocation of dedicated high-frequency AMD EPYC cores paired with a leaner memory profile offers a resource-dense option for workloads that require raw processing speed without the overhead of large memory footprints.

Given the 4.5 GHz clock speed and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D8alds_v7 is suited for compute-bound tasks, batch processing, and web serving workloads that do not demand massive memory arrays. The inclusion of 472 GB of local storage and premium storage compatibility also makes it appropriate for distributed databases, caching layers, and development environments requiring fast local read and write operations.
